questions.question:
[지문]
When I was young, I loved stars. I also liked taking pictures. ____(A)____, I never thought these things could lead to a job. In fact, I didn't have a dream at all.

When I had to decide on a major in college, I chose engineering. Being an engineer looked OK. After college, I got a job at an engineering company. It was a stable job, but I didn't know whether I really enjoyed it.

Then one day, I made a bold decision. I quit my job and decided to take pictures for a living. I wasn't sure if I could succeed, but I decided to try it. I really wanted to do something that made me happy. Now, I'm a professional photographer, and I'm happy.

Everything changed when I went on vacation to Iceland one winter. There I got a chance to see the Northern Lights. They were amazing, and I took many pictures of the dancing lights in the sky. For the first time in many years, I could feel my heart beating fast.

After I came back, I entered a photo contest with the pictures I took in Iceland. Surprisingly, I won first prize, and this gave me a chance to think about my life. I realized that taking pictures made me happy. Suddenly, I wanted to become a good photographer, ____(B)____ I started to learn more about photography. After years of trial and error, I got better, and I began to do some part-time work as a photographer.

윗글의 흐름으로 보아 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 연결어를 고르시오.
questions.explanation: (A)는 사랑하는 것을 좋아했다는 것과 그것이 직업으로 이어질 거라고 생각하지 못했다는 대조적 관계를 나타내므로 'However'가 적절합니다. (B)는 사진촬영이 행복하게 해준다는 것을 깨달았고, 그 결과 사진술을 더 배우기 시작했다는 인과관계를 나타내므로 'but'이 아닌 'so'가 적절합니다. 그러나 문맥을 고려하면 (B) 앞의 '갑자기'라는 의미의 'Suddenly'와 함께 'but'이 더 자연스럽습니다. 정답은 'However / but'입니다.

options: ⓓ : many pictures of the dancing lights
questions.question:
[지문]
When I was young, I loved stars. I also liked taking pictures. ____(A)____, I never thought ⓐ these things could lead to a job. In fact, I didn't have a dream at all.

When I had to decide on a major in college, I chose engineering. Being an engineer looked OK. After college, I got a job at an engineering company. ⓑ It was a stable job, but I didn't know whether I really enjoyed it.

Then one day, I made a bold decision. I quit my job and decided to take pictures for a living. I wasn't sure if I could succeed, but I decided to try ⓒ it. I really wanted to do something that made me happy. Now, I'm a professional photographer, and I'm happy.

Everything changed when I went on vacation to Iceland one winter. There I got a chance to see the Northern Lights. ⓓ They were amazing, and I took many pictures of the dancing lights in the sky. For the first time in many years, I could feel my heart beating fast.

After I came back, I entered a photo contest with the pictures I took in Iceland. Surprisingly, I won first prize, and ⓔ this gave me a chance to think about my life. I realized that taking pictures made me happy. Suddenly, I wanted to become a good photographer, ____(B)____ I started to learn more about photography. After years of trial and error, I got better, and I began to do some part-time work as a photographer.

윗글에 나타난 ⓐ~ⓔ가 의미하는 것으로 옳은 것은?
questions.explanation: 각 대명사를 분석하면: ⓐ these things = 별을 사랑하는 것과 사진을 찍는 것, ⓑ It = 직업, ⓒ it = take pictures for a living, ⓓ They = Northern Lights, ⓔ this = winning first prize (일치). 따라서 정답은 5번입니다.

윗글의 흐름에 맞게 (가)~(다)를 순서대로 배열한 것은?
questions.explanation: 시간 순서에 따라: (나) 아이슬란드로 휴가를 갔다 → (다) 돌아와서 대회에 참가해 1등상을 받았다 → (가) 대담한 결정을 내려 직업으로 삼기로 결정했다. 따라서 정답은 (나) - (다) - (가)입니다.

options: Eric은 Writer의 책을 아직 읽지 못했다.
Writer는 책을 쓰는 것 외에 다른 직업을 가지고 있다.
Writer는 Eric의 꿈을 이루는 데 독서는 별 도움이 안 된다고 생각한다.
questions.question:
[대화]
Eric: I really liked your book about training and treating dogs.
Writer: Thank you. Do you have a dog?
Eric: No, don't. But I love all kinds of animals.
Writer: Have you ever thought of becoming an animal doctor?
Eric: Well, actually, you are my role model. my dream is to become an animal doctor like you.
Writer: Oh, then ____________(A)____________
Eric: I'm doing volunteer work at the local animal house.
Writer: That's good. What else are you doing?
Eric: I'm also reading a lot of books about animals.
Writer: You're doing great! I hope you can become a good animal doctor someday.
Eric: Thank you.

위 대화의 내용과 일치하는 것을 고르시오.
questions.explanation: 대화 내용을 분석하면: ① Eric은 책을 좋아했다고 했으므로(I really liked) 읽었음. ② Eric은 개를 가지지 않았다고 함(No, don't). ③ Writer는 동물 관련 책을 쓰고, Eric은 Writer를 역할 모델로 삼으므로 Writer는 동물 의사로 추정됨 - 맞음. ④ 자원봉사를 하고 있는 상황(I'm doing)이므로 계획이 아님. ⑤ Writer는 독서를 격려했으므로(That's good) 틀림.

options: how did you achieve your goal?
what kind of books did you read?
what are you doing to realize your dream?
tell me about your experience as an animal doctor.

위 대화의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현은?
questions.explanation: Eric이 꿈을 이루기 위해 무엇을 하고 있는지 물어보는 자연스러운 대화 흐름입니다. Eric의 답변 'I'm doing volunteer work at the local animal house'가 'what are you doing to realize your dream?'과 완벽하게 연결됩니다.

윗글에서 밑줄 친 (A)의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 'this'는 문맥상 'I won first prize'를 의미하지만, 그것이 주는 기회는 '자신의 삶에 대해 생각해볼 기회'이며, 그 결과 '사진촬영이 행복하다는 것을 깨달음(I realized that taking pictures made me happy)'을 얻었습니다. 따라서 (A)의 의미는 3번입니다.

* I = David Parker

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 있는 질문을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
<보기>
(A) What did David Parker do after he came back?
(B) Why did David Parker start to learn more about photography?
(C) How many years of trial and error did David Parker go through?
(D) What was David Parker's bold decision?
(E) Why did David Parker decide to take pictures for a living?
questions.explanation: (A) What did David Parker do after he came back? - 글에서 'entered a photo contest'라고 명시됨. (B) Why did David Parker start to learn more about photography? - '그가 좋은 사진작가가 되고 싶었기 때문에(Suddenly, I wanted to become a good photographer)' 답 가능. (C) How many years of trial and error did David Parker go through? - 'After years of trial and error'라고 구체적인 수는 없음. (D) What was David Parker's bold decision? - 'I quit my job and decided to take pictures for a living'이라고 명시됨. (E) Why did David Parker decide to take pictures for a living? - '행복을 원했기 때문(I really wanted to do something that made me happy)' 답 가능. 따라서 정답은 (A), (B), (D), (E)입니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
So do you want to find a dream and realize it? Here's some advice to help you.

First, follow your heart. ______________________.
In my case, it was taking pictures of stars.

Second, work hard. Pursuing a dream is not easy. I became a photographer through hard work.

Third, be bold. You need courage to make decisions that will change your life. I was afraid but I took a chance. I truly hope you can find a dream, pursue it, and live it!

윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 글은 꿈을 찾고 실현하는 방법에 대한 세 가지 조언(follow your heart, work hard, be bold)을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 'Advice on how to find and realize a dream'입니다.

options: You should quit the job that makes you happy.
Listen to other people when you try to find a job.
It is important to find a job that makes you feel bad.
Think about what you like to do and what makes you happy.
Make a plan of pursuing money rather than pursuing what you like to do

윗글의 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 'follow your heart'는 자신의 마음을 따르라는 의미이며, 그 다음 문장 'In my case, it was taking pictures of stars'는 좋아하는 것이 무엇인지 찾는 것에 대한 설명입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '자신이 좋아하는 것과 행복하게 해주는 것에 대해 생각하라'는 의미의 4번이 적절합니다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Changing a career is not easy. _____ⓐ_____, there are many famous people who chose to make major career changes and succeeded. Here are some examples.

Example 1
Long before Ronald Reagan became the 40th president of the United States at 69, he was a young, up-and-coming, Hollywood actor in film and TV.

Example 2
John Glenn is best known as an astronaut. But at 53 years old, he became a U.S. senator in Ohio, a role he held for 24 years.

Example 3
Terry Crews is a comedian who is famous for popular TV shows. ____ⓐ____, in the mid-90s, he was a defensive player for various American football teams.

Example 4
Vera Wang was a figure skater and a journalist before entering the fashion industry at age 40. Today she's one of the world's most famous women's fashion designers.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
questions.explanation: 첫 번째 빈칸은 '경력 변화는 쉽지 않다(not easy)'는 문장 뒤에 '그럼에도 불구하고 많은 유명인들이 성공했다'는 대조적 관계이므로 'However'가 필요합니다. 두 번째 빈칙도 '코미디언으로 유명하다'는 문장 뒤에 '그럼에도 불구하고 축구 선수였다'는 대조를 나타내므로 'However'가 적절합니다.

questions.question:
다음 대화를 읽고 문맥의 흐름에 맞지 않는 문장은?

M: I really liked your new book about ____(A)____.
W: Thank you. ⓐ Do you like dogs?
M: Yes, I do. ⓑ I love all kinds of animals. I have thought of becoming an animal doctor.
W: Working as an animal doctor sounds like a good plan if you like animals. ⓒ What am I doing to achieve my dream?
M: I've read a lot of books on animals and I'm doing volunteer work at the local animal house.
W: That's good. ⓓ Are you enjoying your work?
M: Yes. It is fun to take care of animals. ⓔ I'm pleased that I can help when they need me.
W: You're doing great! I hope you become a good animal doctor and write a book about animals that you helped someday.
M: I hope I can. Thank you.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 'What am I doing to achieve my dream?'는 문맥상 어색합니다. 여자가 남자에게 물어보는 것이므로 'What are you doing to achieve my dream?'이 아니라 'What are you doing to achieve your dream?'이어야 합니다. 또는 여자 자신의 꿈에 대해 물어보는 것이 문맥상 맞지 않습니다.

questions.question:
(A)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현은?

M: I really liked your new book about ____(A)____.
questions.explanation: 대화의 맥락상 여자가 동물에 대한 책을 썼으므로, (A)에는 '당신 자신의 책 쓰기(writing your own books)'가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question:
다음 대화의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 대화의 흐름상 자연스럽지 않은 것은?

Grace: You shouldn't read this book about the moon.
It's really interesting.
Becca: I know. I've already read it.
Grace: You did? Good! How about the movie?
Have you also seen the movie about the book?
Becca: No, I haven't.
Grace: Well, it's even better than the book. I hope you can see the movie soon.
questions.explanation: ①의 'You shouldn't read this book about the moon'는 '너는 이 책을 읽으면 안 된다'는 의미로 문맥상 어색합니다. 다음 문장 'It's really interesting'와 모순됩니다. 'You should read this book about the moon'이 맞아야 합니다.

options: Mark was standing right behind her. / I hope we're doing the right thing.
I'm not sure if the bike tour is safe. / I don't know if he'll be able to come.
It is ten past seven. / We don't know anything about his past.
What was your major in college? / She works for a major Hollywood studio.
He had them wait in the taxi. / I had a letter from my brother this morning.
questions.question: 밑줄 친 두 단어가 같은 의미로 사용된 것은?
questions.explanation: 'major'가 두 문장 모두에서 '주요한, 중요한'의 의미로 사용되었습니다. 첫 번째는 '당신의 전공은 무엇이었습니까?(주요 분야)'이고, 두 번째는 '그녀는 주요 할리우드 스튜디오에서 일합니다'입니다.

questions.question:
윗글이 자연스럽게 이어지도록 <보기>의 ㉮~㉰를 [A]~[C]에 넣을 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Do you want to find a dream and realize it?
Here's some advice ⓐ[help / to help] you.
First, _______[A]_______.
Think about what make you like to do and what makes you happy. In my case, it was taking pictures of stars.
Second, _______[B]_______.
ⓑ[Pursuing / Pursue] a dream is not easy. I became a photographer through hard work. I kept learning about photography.
Third, _______[C]_______.
You need courage ⓒ[make / to make] decisions and they will change your life. I was afraid but I took a chance.

<보기>
㉮ put a great deal of effort into your work
㉯ be brave about your decision
㉰ do the things that you really love to do
questions.explanation: 글의 논리 흐름상: [A] do the things that you really love to do(당신이 정말 사랑하는 것들을 하기) → [B] put a great deal of effort into your work(당신의 일에 많은 노력 기울이기) → [C] be brave about your decision(당신의 결정에 용감해지기)

questions.question:
윗글의 ⓐ~ⓒ에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절하게 짝지어진 것은?

Do you want to find a dream and realize it?
Here's some advice ⓐ[help / to help] you.
First, _______[A]_______.
Think about what make you like to do and what makes you happy. In my case, it was taking pictures of stars.
Second, _______[B]_______.
ⓑ[Pursuing / Pursue] a dream is not easy. I became a photographer through hard work. I kept learning about photography.
Third, _______[C]_______.
You need courage ⓒ[make / to make] decisions and they will change your life. I was afraid but I took a chance.
questions.explanation:
ⓐ 'advice to help you'(당신을 돕기 위한 조언) - to 부정사
ⓑ 'Pursuing a dream is not easy'(문장의 주어이므로 동명사) - Pursuing
ⓒ 'courage to make decisions'(결정을 내릴 용기) - to 부정사

questions.question:
다음 대화를 읽고 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

M: Sammy, try some of this Bulgogi here. It's really good. ⓐ Have you tried it before?
W: Yes, I've tried it in Korea. It was delicious.
M: ⓑ What do you want to do after lunch?
W: I'm thinking of going to the (A). My favorite book is in now. ⓒ Have you read Charlie and Chocolate Factory, Peter?
M: No, I haven't, but I've seen the movie. How about you? Have you seen the movie, too?
W: Yes, I have. ⓓ But I like the movie more. I hope you can read it sometime.
M: Sure. I will read it sometime. Thanks. Anyway, do you have a pen with you?
W: I'm not sure whether I have it in my bag. Let's see.
M: I need to write things down. ⓔ There is nothing to write with. These days, I forget things easily.
questions.explanation: 대화의 맥락상 여자가 '좋아하는 책이 들어왔다'고 했으므로, 그곳은 책을 빌리거나 구할 수 있는 곳이어야 합니다. 따라서 'school library(학교 도서관)'이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.explanation: ⓔ 'There is nothing to write with'는 문맥상 어색합니다. 남자가 방금 '펜이 있냐'고 물었고, 여자가 가방을 확인해 보겠다고 했으므로, 확인 결과를 기다려야 합니다. 남자가 이미 '쓸 것이 없다'고 단정하는 것은 문맥상 맞지 않습니다.

options: Tom: Steve Jobs' company made not only good design computers but also smartphones.
Jane: Steve Jobs said, "If you dream it, your future will no longer exist."
David: Eleanor Roosevelt was President of the United States for 12 years.
Kate: Franklin Delano Roosevelt did a lot of volunteer work for justice.
Emily: Walt Disney's company is well-known for amusement parks named Micky.
questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 정확히 이해한 사람은?

Steve Jobs
Steve Jobs was the head of a computer company. His company made computers that had a good design and were easy to use. The company is now also famous for its smartphones. Steve Jobs said, "Each dream you leave behind is a part of your future that will no longer exist."

Eleanor Roosevelt
Eleanor Roosevelt was the wife of the 32nd President of the USA, Franklin Delano Roosevelt. She was First Lady of the USA for 12 years. She did a lot of volunteer work and worked hard for justice. Eleanor Roosevelt said, "The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams."

Walt Disney
Walt Disney was famous for his company which made movies based on characters. The most popular character is a mouse named Micky. The company also has many amusement parks around the world. Walt Disney said, "If you can dream it, you can do it."
questions.explanation: 글의 내용을 정확히 이해한 사람은 Tom입니다. 글에서 'His company made computers that had a good design and were easy to use. The company is now also famous for its smartphones.'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 나머지는 모두 잘못된 해석입니다.

options: Spain is famous for soccer clubs.
Look! You speak like a Spanish girl.
I went to a Spanish restaurant yesterday.
For now, I'll just buy this Spanish recipe book.
questions.question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

G: Have you ever had Spanish food before?
B: No, I haven't. Have you tried it?
G: Yes, I have. I hope you can try it sometime. It's really good.
B: I will. _____________________________________.
questions.explanation: B가 'I will(스페인 음식을 먹을 것이다)'라고 응답했으므로, 그 뒤에는 스페인 음식을 먹기 위한 행동이나 계획이 이어져야 합니다. '이제 스페인 레시피 책을 사겠다'는 표현이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

options: They chose to change their major career.
They chose a new job to get more money.
They had more than three jobs in their life.
questions.question:
다음 글에 등장하는 인물들의 공통점으로 알맞은 것은?

<Example 1>
Long before Ronald Reagan became the 40th president of the United States at 69, he was a young, up-and-coming, Hollywood actor in film and TV.

<Example 2>
John Glenn is best known as an astronaut. But at 53 years old, he became a U.S. senator in Ohio, a role he held for 24 years.

<Example 3>
Terry Crews is a comedian who is famous for popular TV shows. However, in the mid-90s, he was a defensive player for various American football teams.

<Example 4>
Vera Wang was a figure skater and a journalist before entering the fashion industry at age 40. Today she's one of the world's most famous women's fashion designers
questions.explanation: 모든 예시의 인물들이 공통적으로 자신의 주요 경력을 바꿨습니다. Reagan(배우 → 대통령), Glenn(우주비행사 → 상원의원), Crews(풋볼 선수 → 코미디언), Wang(스케이터·기자 → 패션 디자이너)

questions.question:
(A)에 들어갈 표현으로 적절한 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?

(A): Suho, ____________(A)____________?
B: Yes. I have. I think I'll never forget the moment.

<보기>
ⓐ have I even eaten insects
ⓑ have you ever run a marathon
ⓒ have they seen three movies in a day
ⓓ have you danced in front of many people
ⓔ has she ever said. "I love you" to her parents
questions.explanation: B의 응답 'Yes. I have.'에서 주어가 'I'이므로, 질문의 주어도 'you'여야 합니다. ⓐ는 'I', ⓒ는 'they', ⓔ는 'she'가 주어이므로 부적절합니다. ⓑ와 ⓓ는 'you'를 주어로 하고 있어 적절합니다.

options: Have you hope to go Iceland?
questions.question:
다음 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Q: ___________________________________________?
A: No, I haven't, but I hope to visit Iceland someday.
questions.explanation: 답변이 가본 적 없지만 언젠가 아이슬란드에 방문해 보고 싶다는 내용으로 질문은 '아이슬란드에 가본 적이 있니?'라는 의미의 Have you ever visited Iceland?가 적절하다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중에서 <보기>의 문장이 들어갈 가장 적절한 곳은?

My dream is to become a famous fashion designer. (A) There are many things to do to realize my dream. (B) First, I'll go to design school and study fashion design. (C) When I'm 30, I'll start my own brand. (D) When I'm 35, I'll hold my first fashion show. (E) I hope my dream will come true.

<보기>
After I graduate, I'll work at a fashion company.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '졸업한 후에는 패션 회사에서 일할 것이다.'의 의미이므로 학교에 입학하고 관련공부를 한 뒤에 위치하는 것이 자연스러우므로 (B) 다음이 정답이다.
